spec: specs/M2.md 4.5, re-measured with the real M2.1 pipeline (src/file/client.ts)

methods.page: spike/m2-take.html + spike/m2-take.ts: analyseFile(file) from src/file/client.ts, result held on the main thread until the tail of sampling ends.
methods.fileInput: Playwright setInputFiles on <input type=file>; decodeFile reads File.arrayBuffer().
methods.decode: src/file/decode.ts. WAV at 44.1 or 48 kHz: parseWav (src/take/wav.ts), no decodeAudioData. MP3 and M4A: header rate, decodeAudioData in an OfflineAudioContext at that rate when 44.1 or 48 kHz, else 48 kHz; channels mixed to a Float64Array mono with mixToMono; file bytes and AudioBuffer dropped before returning. decodeMs = analyseFile start to decodeFile resolved (read, parse or decode, mix).
methods.transfer: mono.buffer transferred to a new module Worker (src/file/take.worker.ts), one Worker per job, terminated after the result.
methods.analysis: Worker: analyseTake (src/take/analyse.ts): FrameAnalyzer frames with the continuity decoder (lag Infinity) run as the frames are produced, 0 to 4 kHz power copied into one flat Float32Array from the same FFT, then vibrato spans. Result posted with every typed-array buffer transferred (takeTransferables). analyseMs = post of mono to result received on the main thread (includes Worker start, spectrum, vibrato spans and the transfer). RTF = audio seconds / analyse seconds.
methods.memory: As results/m2_spike.json: renderer phys_footprint lifetime peak from vmmap -summary (verdict), footprint -j about every 200 ms, ps RSS about every 50 ms. Baseline = mean over 4000 ms after a 2500 ms settle with the page loaded (no Worker yet: client.ts starts one per job, the earlier spike page started its Worker on load). Peak window: run plus 1000 ms tail while the page holds the result.
memoryCaveats: phys_footprint counts the renderer only; GPU, browser and utility processes are in the RSS tree column, not in the verdict.
The vmmap lifetime peak has no sampling gaps, but vmmap output is rounded to 0.1 MB and the number includes everything since the renderer started.
RSS leaves out compressed and swapped pages and double-counts shared pages in the tree sum.
Garbage collection timing changes the peak: freed buffers may stay resident until the next GC.
Headless Chrome; a headed tab adds compositor and GPU memory not measured here.
One run per file. The comparison column is a separate run (results/m2_spike.json), so small differences are within run-to-run variation.
